3. When the butter has melted, add the lobsters and cook them in the deep fat in the butter, turning them occasionally, until they turn white and the skin begins to crust, about 8 to 10 minutes.

4. Turn off the heat and take the lobsters out of the butter and add them to the stockpot with the juices and the remaining 2 tbsp of butter (this will make about 4 lobster tails). You can drain them into a colander under running water to stop the liquid from spilling out.

5. Push the lobster tails aside with a spoon and turn the colander upside down into the stockpot to catch the juices.

6. Put the stockpot back on the heat and add the flour to make a roux. Stir the roux into the stock pot, scraping the bottom with a wooden spoon and allow it to brown.

7. Whisk in enough milk to reach a saucepan’s volume. I used about 3 cups. Add herbs, thyme, 1 tbsp butter, salt, pepper and parsley

and mix again.

8. Add 1 cup chopped vegetables such as carrots, celery, potatoes. Let that cook through.

9. Add more minced herbs and the lobster tails and simmer until the sauce has reduced and thickened slightly, probably about 5 -10 minutes.

10. Pour the lobster tails into serving dishes and use 1 tbsp of butter to brush the tops of them.

11. Garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with lemon wedges and butter.

Cheese Bourekas /Bourekas Matah 

2 1/2 cups all purpose flour  

1 1/2 teaspoons salt  

1 (15-ounce) can  well drained crushed tomatoes 

2 tbsp cold water  

3 tbsp olive oil  

6 cups shredded cheddar or other favorite cheese 

6 tbsp margarine or unsalted butter  

1-1/2 tsp salt  

1/4 cup bread crumbs  

1 egg  

8 ounces thinly sliced prosciutto or bacon 

1 cup flour  

1/2 cup cold water  

1 tablespoon olive oil  

2 cups shredded cheddar or any favorite cheese (I’d go with Monterey Jack or Colby)

1.) Put flour and salt in a big bowl and shake off the excess ice water.
2.) Sprinkle tomatoes in and stir to combine.  
3.) Add in olive oil and water and mix very thoroughly.
4.) Let stand for 5 minutes while you prepare the rest of the ingredients.
5.) Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and add Margarine and salt, cooking until it shimmers and becomes nice and golden around the edges.
6.) Remove once done and set aside.
7.) Dip both hands into Margarine and turn dough over several times with them. (Ouchy!). 
8.) Use cold water to lift out and place in a shallow dish. Sprinkle with salt and set aside for 10 minutes. (Another OUCH.)  
9.) Cut dough into three sections: the first will make the top of each piece of dough, the second will join them together for the base, and the last will be turned inside-out. Flatten them as best you can. 
10.) Cut the bottom into three pieces as shown.
11.) Take one of the pieces of dough and lay it horizontally. Spread one cup’s worth of salted tomato marmelade on the outside edge. 
12.) Grab the base of that piece and lay it with the other pieces facing outwards, along the length of the edge all the way to the side. Pinch the corners together to close it up and press in the heel of an open hand and do the same with the top piece. 
13.) Cut a ½-inch wide “X” into the middle with a paring knife.
14.) Roll the second piece of dough up from the center outwards to make a rectangle about 7″ X8″
15.) Press down slightly with your right hand.
16.) Place one cup of shredded cheddar and an equal amount of salt in the middle of the rectangle with the open side down.
17.) Carefully take the loose edge of the rectangle (the one with the “X”) and fold over the two points at the top. 
18.) Pull the bottom edge down and press down as you open it to form a half-moon shape with the open side facing down. (Open side will show.) 
19.) Cut the corners off (with knife) to create the classic “baguette” shape. 
20.) Place half an inch of cheese mixture in the middle (without overlap) from edge to edge and fold back the bottom three quarters of the rectangle.
21.) Roll out the other half of the remaining dough on a lightly floured surface. Fold it over the top and bottom of the rectangle, then open it and roll back to the original size and shape. Cut with scissors around the rectangle and into a 3-foot log. If you are going to wrap it for transport, cut the ends of the log into 6 inch long pieces.
22.) Cut out a hole in the middle of one end and lay the prosciutto or bacon in it, making sure that is tucked inside. (The bacon should be completely covered.)
23.) Transfer bourekas to a cookie sheet and bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 20-25 minutes, or until a nice golden brown. 
24.) Remove the prosciutto or bacon and sprinkle the top with bread crumbs. Once they have cooled completely, cut through the top, opening it and putting two small strips of prosciutto or bacon inside, as shown.
